boundary: which layer makes a PHP 5.0.0 defect visible: emalloc's cache and 8-byte rounding hide it from any detector at free() (asan-blind, the nested allocator), or efree reaches free() and the libc boundary sees it (temporal-asan-visible). Decided per case by MEASUREMENT: ASan with the allocator patched versus ASan with it as shipped, both run here
title: PHP 5.0.0 memory-safety defects in the engine and ext/standard, as script triggers through the real interpreter, split by whether the Zend allocator hides them
note: Derived, not retyped: tools/build-cases.py writes every case from the collaborator's php-5.0.0-bug-corpus (185 cases; zip sha256 31d22a3b468e96e0ff9f991d8667e78a..., not in this repository) and from OUR three native runs of its 127 default-build cases (ASan with PHP's allocator patched, ASan with it as shipped, the plain build), on which each case's population and oracle.json rest. 48 asan-blind and 22 temporal-asan-visible here, 70 cases. The first build gave 65, 46 and 19, against the collaborator's 31 and 29 on its gcc-13 ASan: 16 cases were placed differently, one (CRASH-100, needs an HTTP listener) is absent, two of theirs (CRASH-062, CRASH-070) end as shipped in PHP's own fatal error with no report, and one (CRASH-064) is a use-after-free NEITHER ASan build reports as one -- it dereferences an integer read from a reused object-store bucket, ASan:SEGV on both -- so those three were in neither population; each said in its PROVENANCE.md. The merge with the sibling corpus (2026-10-28) widened the temporal rule and admitted five as cases 66 to 70: CRASH-062 and -070 as asan-blind, CRASH-012, -148 (CWE-590) and -161 (CWE-415) as temporal-asan-visible. CRASH-064 is still in neither. The fourth configuration run-realphp.py drives, php-real-stock, is the judge's control (nothing revoked), not a case arm. The default-build cases outside both populations (spatial defects ASan sees unaided, NULL dereferences, type confusions) are not here yet.
